doc.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011

title: A bad bass player hired in Denver for Rawls
summary: He hired a Denver bass player sight unseen and the gigs were awful.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Before we sort of move on from there, is there any particular train wreck stories about any of those gigs that you want to talk about? Or great gigs?

Well the train wreck gig, actually luckily we didn’t get that many of them. There were one of two times, I remember with Lou Rawls our bass player was going to leave and so © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -13-

we were going to be in Denver. We didn’t have a bass player, and we were looking to get a permanent replacement. So there was a fella that was a bass player in Albany that I’d worked with, his son had located to Denver and apparently was working out there. Now this bass player that I knew was very, very good. And I didn’t know what the son was, but I was assuming that he was a good bass player. So I got his number from Dad and called him up and said “look, we’re going to be doing a gig in Denver, we need a bass player. You want to come on? If it works out you can have the gig, with Lou Rawls. And he said “yeah, you know, I’d like to try that.” And he was absolutely — not only was he not very good, he was scared stiff. And so the rehearsal was just — I don’t know how we’re going to do this. And of course we rehearsed in the afternoon of the gig, because that’s traditional. You’ve got a gig that starts at 8, you rehearse from 2 to 4, shower and come on. Okay. So I warned him a little ahead of time. I said “this guy’s not very good so we’ll just get through these two nights.” So he wasn’t very good. He blew just about everything. And I kept asking “turn down” so people can’t hear you, and we got through two shows that night and two the next night and it was just horrible.
And then you had to call Dad.

Oh yes. And there were words there, you know “why did you hire this guy?” Well because, and it’s just kind of a hard situation. Unless you know for sure the musician’s abilities, you take a chance. I took a chance on factors that didn’t actually make any difference. I never heard him play. So I just trusted. And again, you know you’re in a situation where just about every musician you meet on that road circuit, they’re all good. It’s unusual to find somebody that’s in that circuit that isn’t like great. So you can come across somebody that’s in there but he wasn’t really in there. Okay. So that was a bad gig.
